newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT/ITT seen back on track after 1997.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT/ITT seen back on track after 1997.

text.p: Construction-related disruptions at ITT Corp's casinos that helped to wipe out the company's third quarter earnings growth are expected to continue to plague the company until the end of 1997.

Analysts said bad luck at ITT's baccarat tables and construction at its two Las Vegas casinos, which deterred gamblers, dented third quarter results and have caused Wall Street to worry that increased competition in the industry will spill over to other casino companies in the form of earnings disappointments.

ITT shares tumbled eight to 48 by late Tuesday and most big-capitalization operators fell in sympathy: Hilton Hotels Corp dropped 1-1/8 to 105, Circus Circus Enterprises Inc lost 1/4 to 34, Mirage Resorts Inc shed 1/4 to 23-1/2 and Bally Entertainment Corp declined 1/4 to 26-3/4.

"News of the the weakness at ITT has hammered the entire sector. Wall Street tends to paint all the gaming stocks with the same brush, so the selloff is somewhat overdone," said Thomas Ryan, BT Securities gaming analyst.
After Monday's market close, ITT said third quarter income will about equal the year-ago quarter's $0.56 per share because of bacarrat losses and construction-related disruptions.
Wall Street was expecting about $0.80 per share.
Jason Ader, Bears Stearns gaming analyst, said he "continues to believe that there are substantial growth prospects for ITT in 1998 and beyond."
Ader, who lowered ITT to attractive from buy, emphasized that the bacarrat losses are "not a Las Vegas market problem."
Analysts continued to urge selective investing in the sector, which has been hit hard with sharp declines in the last three three months as growing competition squeezes income and profit margins.
Because of rising competition, analysts have the greatest confidence in large operators with experienced managements, like Circus Circus, Mirage and Hilton.
As for ITT, which had also been widely recommended, the analysts' earnings views were quickly pared after ITT issued its warning.
While Salomon Bros gaming analyst Bruce Turner said his strong buy recommendation remains, he said $0.10 to $0.15 of his third quarter $0.20 estimate cut to $0.58 per share is based on bad luck.
ITT said part of its third quarter net has ended up in the pockets of high-stakes baccarat players who beat the house -- Caesars Palace -- in August.
The revision was also attributed to decreased gaming activity at ITT's two Las Vegas properties because ongoing construction projects have reduced the number of gamblers.
The Palace and the Sheraton Dessert Inn are undergoing facelifts and expansions, and ITT said some gamblers choose other Strip gaming halls when they see the construction.

Also, Turner allocated $0.03 to $0.05 of the cut to ITT's acknowledgement of sharply lower EBITDA at its Tunica, Miss., casino, hurt by competition from new casinos opened by Harrah's Entertainment Inc and Grand Casinos Inc. "ITT has short-term problems in Las Vegas and the news has given the company a wake-up call to accelerate construction of rooms at Casear's Palace. But the biggest culprit was that they got killed on high-end play," Ryan said.

"What they want to do (with the newly-constructed capacity) is to get the regular Las Vegas slot player, the type of operation that smooths out revenue flow," Ryan said. "Casinos like high-end play, put Wall Street does not because it is not predictable."
ITT, he said, joins a list of operators including Boyd Gaming Corp and Harrah's that have "reported weak quarters based (partly) on Tunica."
But in the long run, ITT is a great story, Ryan said. He said the company is expected to post 20 percent year-over-year earnings gains after 1997.
-- Wall Street Desk, 212-859-1734
